Hi Maria —

Thanks again for the call today. As discussed, I’m sending a draft Mutual Action Plan that lays out the staged approval gates we usually use for enterprise procurement (evaluation -> security sign-off -> commercial/finance -> legal execution), and how the MSA / DPA / order form dependencies fit into a 6–8 week close timeline.

Attached: Nimble_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP with dates and owners), plus a PDF with our current MSA markups for reference.

Top-level notes:
- We recommend splitting legal review into two parallel tracks: (1) commercial/order form negotiation (pricing, PO terms) and (2) MSA/DPA redlines. In our experience, moving the commercial/order form to signature first (with a contract clause that references the pending MSA) materially shortens time-to-production.
- Security review (SOC2 and data handling questions) is typically the gating item for DPA sign-off; we can provide a SOC2 package snapshot and a short control matrix.
- Proposed milestone dates are conservative; if Nimble can commit to 2 internal reviewers per track we can accelerate by ~10 days.

Action items I propose for the MAP spreadsheet:
1) Nimble to confirm internal reviewers for Security and Legal by 2026-05-18.
2) Redwood to accept commercial order form term sheet and provide final PO-ready document by 2026-05-21.
3) Legal tracks to exchange redlines: MSA/DPA redlines back from Nimble by 2026-05-28.
4) Target signature (order form + MSA) by 2026-06-04, contingent on DPA clarifications.

Would you prefer we split the MAP into an accelerated 4-week lane and the conservative 8-week lane? I included both in the spreadsheet.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short review call.

Maria / Carlos —

Thanks — good questions. Short answers below and I’ve updated the MAP to call out the specific dependencies you flagged. I pasted the key sections inline for quick scanning.

1) SOC2 & evidence pack
- We can provide a current SOC2 Type II bridge letter and a targeted control matrix that maps the DPA articles to our audit controls. I attached a one-page SOC2 snapshot to the shared Drive link for your security team.

2) MSA redlines (indemnity cap & data residency)
- Indemnity cap: our standard is an industry-tiered cap aligned to annualized fees; we can provisionally offer a compromise cap for the initial order form period and re-evaluate at renewal.
- Data residency: we support region pinning for model serving on Dedicated and can include a residency statement in the DPA scope. For GCP eu-west workloads we’ll document the deployed region and associated controls.

3) Order form first approach (commercial-first / MSA to follow)
- We use an \"Order Form First\" pattern occasionally. The MAP now includes a fallback clause template: the order form is conditioned on execution of a final MSA within X days (we usually use 30 days) or, alternatively, the order form contains a limited scope SOW and a mutual termination right if MSA is not signed in time. This reduces procurement lag while protecting both parties.

Updated MAP highlights (excerpt):
- Gate A (Evaluation): Proof-of-concept sign-off -> security checklist completed -> (5 business days)
- Gate B (Commercial): Order form finalization & PO issuance -> (target net 7 days)
- Gate C (Legal): MSA/DPA redlines converged -> final signatures (target within 30 days of PO)

Proposed timeline (accelerated lane) — assuming Nimble provides two named reviewers per track:
- 2026-05-18: Nimble internal reviewers named
- 2026-05-21: Redwood delivers PO-ready order form
- 2026-05-25: Procurement completes commercial review and issues PO
- 2026-05-28: MSA/DPA redlines received from Nimble
- 2026-06-04: Signatures (order form + MSA) / handoff to onboarding

Action items for this thread:
- Carlos / Nimble Legal: confirm if a 30-day MSA window is acceptable or propose alternative.
- Procurement: confirm PO path and whether pre-signed order forms are allowed.
- Security: confirm if the SOC2 snapshot + control matrix suffices or whether you need a deeper artifact.

If useful we can run a 30-minute close-plan working session tomorrow to walk the MAP and allocate owners. Ava and Stephanie from my team will be on the call to handle the technical and legal handoffs.

Thanks —
Aditya
